walkthroughs.body_html:
Vectors & Transformation Geometry — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Vectors & Transformation Geometry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Vectors & Transformation Geometry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How do you add the column vectors (3,4) and (1,-2)?
options: Multiply the components to get (3, -8).
Add all four numbers to get a single value, 6.
By multiplying the components: 3 x 4 = 12.
Add the components separately to get (4, 2).

mcqs.q: How is the magnitude of vector (3,4) found?
options: Using Pythagoras: the square root of (3 squared + 4 squared) = 5.
By multiplying the components: 3 x 4 = 12.
By adding the components: 3 + 4 = 7.
It rotates the vector by 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: What does multiplying a vector by a scalar do?
options: It only changes the first component.
By multiplying the components: 3 x 4 = 12.
It rotates the vector by 90 degrees.
It multiplies each component by the scalar, changing the vector's length while keeping its direction (reversed if negative).
